title: Hiring Mosaic: Compact Interview Rubric + 14-Day Micro-Onboard
content:
Purpose

This note captures a compact, reusable interview rubric and an adjacent 14-day micro-onboard curriculum designed for rapid hires across early-stage pods (product, infra, serving runtime). The goal: reduce time-to-impact for mid-senior ICs by combining calibrated interview signals with a focused, measurable first-14-days plan. Use this as a lightweight canonical artifact for hiring panels and for hiring managers to hand off to mentors once an offer is accepted.

Scope and intended users
- People Ops: standardize interviewer training and feedback formats.
- Hiring managers and interviewers: quick reference to score consistently.
- New-hire mentors and EMs: plug the 14-day micro-onboard into team onboarding.

Quick guidance on use
1) Interviewers should spend ~10–15 minutes writing evidence mapped to rubric anchors (not just a score).
2) Scores alone are noisy; weigh candidate signals: impact, problem solving clarity, hireability (culture/communication), and role fit.
3) Hiring committee uses aggregated evidence & rubric to surface risks and gap mitigation plans.

Competency dimensions (compact)
1) Problem Decomposition (PD) — ability to structure ambiguous problems, propose tractable milestones.
2) Technical Craft (TC) — depth of system knowledge, appropriate tradeoffs, debugging/synthesis capability.
3) Ownership & Delivery (OD) — history of delivering features, release thinking, and follow-through.
4) Collaboration & Communication (CC) — cross-team communication, priming, and feedback receptivity.
5) Culture & Coachability (CCB) — alignment to company norms (customer-first, pragmatic), openness to feedback.

Scoring scale (1–5) and anchor prompts (compact)
- 5 (Exceptional): Clear, repeatable examples; demonstrates pattern-recognition; proposes measurable delivery plan.
- 4 (Strong): Good technical depth and pragmatic choices with limited clarifying questions.
- 3 (Meets bar): Solves core problem with some gaps; needs ramping but feasible.
- 2 (Borderline): Partial approach; concerning gaps in breadth or delivery evidence.
- 1 (Insufficient): Fails to produce workable approach or lacks fundamental knowledge.

Evidence anchors (what to capture)
- PD: Outline of decomposition, trade-offs considered, checkpoints for success.
- TC: Concrete examples of architectures/algorithms used, perf / cost tradeoffs, debugging story.
- OD: Stories with timelines, stakeholders, endpoints delivered, post-launch monitoring.
- CC: Examples of cross-team negotiation, async communication artifacts (PRs, RFCs).
- CCB: Past feedback loops, examples of learning from mistake, mentorship interactions.

Sample role-specific weightings (for panel leads to adopt)
- Serving Runtime Engineer: PD 20%, TC 35%, OD 25%, CC 10%, CCB 10%
- Developer Experience / SDK: PD 15%, TC 25%, OD 20%, CC 30%, CCB 10%
- Product Manager (IC): PD 25%, TC 10%, OD 30%, CC 25%, CCB 10%

Behavioral probe examples (short)
- PD: "Walk me through a time you turned a vague performance problem into a reproducible ticket and a rollout plan."
- TC: "Describe a time you diagnosed a production perf regression; what root causes did you rule out and how?"
- OD: "Tell me about a shipped feature where metrics changed unexpectedly post launch — what did you do?"
- CC: "How have you handled misalignment with a partner team during a critical milestone? Be specific."
- CCB: "Share a candid example when feedback changed how you work."

Bias-mitigation & anchoring notes
- Ask for concrete outcomes (numbers, timelines) rather than subjective adjectives.
- Prefer evidence over narrative: if candidate claims ownership, ask for PRs, metrics, or specific collaborators.
- Calibrate panels regularly (monthly quick syncs) using 2–3 anonymized past interviews as examples.

Feedback template (2–3 sentences)
- Start: one-line summary of candidate fit (hire/no-hire/ambiguous + top signal).
- Middle: 2 bullets of evidence mapped to competencies.
- End: explicit risk and mitigation recommendation (e.g., "strong hire if paired with 30-day mentoring on X").

-- 14-Day Micro-Onboard Curriculum (purpose: launch to deliverable) --
Principles: low-friction, outcome-oriented, measurable checkpoints. Each day includes an explicit owner (mentor or EM), expected artifacts, and a success signal. Replace team-specific items as needed.

Pre-Day 0 (offer accepted)
- Deliverables: welcome packet, day-1 agenda, required access checklist, small pre-reads (1 pager on team product & repo map).
- Owner: People Ops + hiring manager.

Day 1: Orientation + Repo Orientation
- Activities: meet EM & mentor, workspace setup, quick repo tour (1–2 key services), launch local dev environment.
- Artifact: PR to touch a trivial file (e.g., README typo) to validate toolchain.
- Success signal: green dev run for the sample service.

Day 2: Observability + Runtime Tour
- Activities: walkthrough of dashboards (latency/cost/alerts), postmortem reading, onboarding ticket assigned.
- Artifact: create a draft improvement ticket for a low-risk perf observation.
- Success signal: ticket created and triaged in backlog.

Day 3: Paired debugging session
- Activities: mentor-led live debug of a flaky test or small production alert replica.
- Artifact: short writeup of root cause & next steps.
- Success signal: reproducer or test added to CI.

Day 4: Ownership boundary mapping
- Activities: map service dependencies and ownership; identify 1st 30-day area of impact.
- Artifact: ownership doc (one page) and an initial 30-day roadmap.
- Success signal: EM signs off on roadmap.

Day 5: Small kickoff project assignment
- Activities: pick a well-scoped 7–14 day task that exercises core infra and delivery path.
- Artifact: scoped PR or spike plan with acceptance criteria.
- Success signal: PR pipeline runs and initial review feedback.

Week 2 focus (days 6–14): deliver the kickoff project, ramp deeper, ship first small change
- Days 6–8: Implement & iterate; daily check-ins with mentor; create tests & perf checks.
- Days 9–11: Internal demo + solicit cross-team feedback; incorporate suggestions.
- Days 12–14: Finalize PR, run post-merge verification, add monitoring alerts where needed.
- Success signal: PR merged, CI green, post-merge smoke test passes, short retrospective doc.

Mentor/EM checklist (first two weeks)
- Daily 30-minute standups for first 5 days, then alternate-day syncs.
- Provide 1 documented code review within 48h.
- Ensure access to production/runbook and at least one end-to-end test.
- Give an early wins memo (what success looks like at 30/60/90 days).

Signals of success by day 14
- Contributed merged change touching core service.
- Demonstrated ability to reproduce a production problem and drive a fix.
- Clear 30-day plan with measurable checkpoints.
- Positive cross-team notes from 2 collaborators.

Red flags to escalate early
- Unable to run local repro or get meaningful infra access within 3 days.
- Evasion on concrete outcomes when asked for examples.
- Repeated inability to accept or act on mentor feedback.

Calibration & continuous improvement
- After each hire, run a 2-week postmortem: did rubric predict ramp? Capture 3 improvements (interview question, rubric anchor, onboarding step).
- Quarterly meta-review: review hires vs ramp time to update role-specific weightings.

Open questions / items to finalize
- Should we add a mandatory short coding challenge for backend ICs (timeboxed to 90 minutes)? Pros/cons listed in linked Confluence.
- Agree on a lightweight anonymized calibration pack (2 historical interviews) for monthly interviewer syncs.

Appendix: quick templates
- Offer handoff note to mentor (one paragraph): role summary, candidate strengths, immediate risk areas, first 3-day checklist.
- Candidate first-week survey (3 questions): Are you unblocked? What would help you be more effective? One improvement idea for the onboarding flow.

Versioning & next steps
- Draft created 2025-11-04 by Sofia Patel.
- Request: People Ops review and one pilot hire using the micro-onboard in Q4 2025.
